$comment: Allow-list for scripts/ci/check-anon-exposure-live.mjs — the sweep that reads
PRODUCTION and asks which relations the public `anon` key can reach.
Two statuses, and they behave differently:
approved      — a human ruled on it. Silent unless it disappears.
grandfathered — exposed when the sweep was built, never explicitly ruled on.
WARNs every run, and ESCALATES to a hard failure if it gains
rows while carrying an identity column.
2026-07-29: the 32 grandfathered entries are GONE, and not by being pardoned —
the Director reviewed them and every one was locked (anon grant revoked; see
migration 20260730000000_revoke_anon_on_grandfathered_relations.sql). The
exposure surface went 36 -> 4. Everything left here is a deliberate, explained
decision, which is the state this file is meant to be in: entries should be
rare and arguable, not a backlog.
Four of those 32 deserve a note, because they read as the opposite of what they
were. pde_certificates, pde_badges, pde_learner_badges and pde_reputation each
carried a policy granting SELECT TO public USING (true) — apparently to serve
the public certificate-verification page at /verify/[number]. They did not.
That page calls /api/certificates/verify, which resolves through
lib/services/certificates/verify-resolver.ts using createServiceRoleClient(),
and service_role bypasses RLS entirely. So the public policy served nothing —
while granting any anonymous visitor the right to enumerate EVERY learner's
certificates, badges and reputation. They were empty, so nothing had leaked.
Locking them was verified not to break verification: /verify/<n> still returns
200 and the API still returns a clean 404 not_found.
TO ADD AN ENTRY: state a reason a stranger can evaluate, and use `approved`
only when somebody actually decided. Guessing here disarms the sweep.
2026-07-31 (second ruling): the sweep flagged 37 more relations. Probing every
one over HTTPS with the public anon key showed 27 actually reachable and 10
refused by an inner guard — a catalog grant is a candidate, not a verdict, and
PostgREST answers a ranged request with 206 on SUCCESS, so counting only 200s
would have under-reported by six. Migration
20260808190000_revoke_anon_on_thirtyone_reporting_views.sql revoked anon on 31
of them (all 27 non-spectator + the 10 that were merely guarded), verified
31/31 returning 401 42501 on the wire afterwards.
The six marathon/tournament/appathon entries below are the exception and are
public ON PURPOSE: the Director confirmed a public event site is planned. The
organiser-internal event views are NOT among them and were revoked — budgets,
sponsor contact details, incident reports and volunteer phone numbers are not
spectator data. If the public event site is ever cancelled, these six should be
revoked too rather than left as inherited defaults.

relations.name: appathon_leaderboard
relations.reason: Director ruling 2026-07-31: team names and scores, the public face of the appathon. Note it reads appathon_verifications, whose own RLS returns 0 rows to anon — so this view is deliberately the published projection of protected data, not an accidental bypass. Wire-verified 200 with 200 rows.

relations.name: audience_vote_summary
relations.reason: Director ruling 2026-07-31: aggregated audience vote tallies per submission, intended for live display. Individual votes stay protected — audience_votes returns 0 rows to anon and only the summary is public. Wire-verified 200 with 551 rows.

relations.name: castes
relations.reason: Read by app/student-form/[token]/ with the BROWSER anon client, by prospective applicants who have no account. Closing it breaks admission intake. Re-proven after the 2026-07-29 lock sweep: still HTTP 200 to an anonymous request, deliberately.

relations.name: community_categories
relations.reason: Same unauthenticated admission-intake path as castes, re-proven 200 in the same check. Closing it breaks sign-ups.

relations.name: feature_usage_summary
relations.reason: Director decision 2026-07-26, same aggregate-statistics ruling as institution_health_scores. Counts of feature use, not rows about identifiable people.

relations.name: institution_health_scores
relations.reason: Director decision 2026-07-26: aggregate, non-personal institution statistics, consciously left open. The rule applied was 'close everything holding personal data; review and consciously rule on the rest'.

relations.name: marathon_categories
relations.reason: Director ruling 2026-07-31: race categories ('10 KM Run') are exactly what a public race page lists. Kept anon-readable deliberately alongside marathon_events. Carries no identity column. Wire-verified 200 with 3 rows.

relations.name: marathon_checkin_summary
relations.reason: Director ruling 2026-07-31: aggregate race-day counter (1,547 registered / 142 checked in), broken down by participating institution. No person is named and no identity column is exposed. Kept for the planned public event site; revisit if the institution breakdown is judged competitive rather than informational. Wire-verified 200 with 11 rows.

relations.name: marathon_events
relations.reason: Director ruling 2026-07-31: a public event site IS planned, and this is the spectator-facing event record (name, date, institution). Kept anon-readable deliberately. Wire-verified 200 with 1 row after the 2026-07-31 revoke sweep, which locked the 8 organiser-internal marathon views (budgets, sponsor contact_email/contact_phone, incidents, committees, tasks, volunteer_phone) around it.

relations.name: tournament_standings
relations.reason: Director ruling 2026-07-31: tournament standings are the point of a public tournament page. Already served publicly through fn_tournament_public_scoreboard on app/p/tournament/[id], which reads it as a SECURITY DEFINER; the direct grant is consistent with that intent rather than an accident. Wire-verified 200 with 4 rows.
